historical_references.reference: Muhafaz was a governorship in the Umayyad Caliphate, centered around modern-day Hama in Syria. It was established in the late 7th century as a buffer state against Byzantine and Christian forces in the region.
historical_references.context: Umayyad Caliphate, Buffer state against Byzantine and Christian forces

historical_references.reference: During the Ayyubid period, Muhafaz was the name of a province in the Levant, comprising areas along the Mediterranean coast from modern-day Syria to Lebanon. It was ruled by the Ayyubid emir Fakhr al-Din II from his capital at Sidon.
historical_references.context: Ayyubid Province, Ruled by Fakhr al-Din II
